nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name:  Eastern mosquitofish
Scientific Name:  Gambusia holbrooki

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum: Chordata
	Class: Osteichthyes
	Order: Atheriniformes
	Family: Poeciliidae

nodes.title: Other Common Names
nodes.body:
Other:	Reference for Scientific Name (Girard 1859)
	Reference for Classification (2377)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Raised in some areas to stock freshwater ponds to control mosquitos.  It is used in the aquarium trade (2368).

Recreational:  This species is kept by hobbyist in home aquaria (2368).

Ecological Role:   The Eastern mosquitofish is the most abundant and ubiquitous fish in fresh water in south Florida (2371).  It is also found in great numbers in brackish waters and has been collected in marginal wetlands of the Indian River Lagoon in salinities as high as 80 ppt (2363).  It is a Keystone species because of its reproductive potential and its ability to alter the habitats in which it occurs (2369).  This mosquitofish is also an abundant food source for piscine and avian predators in numerous shallow habitats (2366; 2371) Gambusia holbrooki is a prime food source for larval and juvenile snook, Centropomus undecimalis in both freshwater and mangrove forest habitats (2366; 2378; 2364).

Indicator:  Associates with aquatic or semiaquatic vegetation, therefore, absence of mosquitofish within indigenous range may denote the absence of wetland vegetated habitat.

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body:
Overall:  In coastal drainages, ponds, and lakes from Mobile Bay east, throughout Florida and north to New Jersey (2376; Wooten et al. 1988).  Gambusia holbrooki Type II of Wooten et al. (1988) is limited to the southeast from the Escambia  River of western Florida to the Altamaha River of eastern Georgia.  Even though Wooten et al. (1988) did not examine Indian River Lagoon populations of Gambusia holbrooki, we assume that they are, in fact, closely related to the St. John's River population and are, therefore, Type II forms of the highly geographically structured species (G. holbrooki/affinis shows the highest heterozygosity reported for fishes, which has significant ecological, demographic, and life history impacts on these species; (2375).  However, Gambusia holbrooki and G. affinis have been introduced throughout the world for mosquito control and may be the most widely distributed freshwater fish world wide (2365).

Within Study Area:  Found in freshwater streams and drainage canals emptying into the Indian River Lagoon; in freshwater and estuarine marshes/mangrove forests, and other peripheral habitats associated with the Indian River Lagoon (848).

Mobility and Migration: The Eastern mosquitofish easily invades new areas as it will follow shallow flowing water fronts associated with ephemeral floods from heavy rains (observed moving down roads; 2372).

Life Mode:  This viviparous euryhaline schooling species typically feeds at or near the surface in shallow, still or slow moving waters generally associated with emergent vegetation or other structures (2365; 2363; 2371).  They may move offshore at night and may be found in water up to 3.6 m in depth.

nodes.title: Habitat Type
nodes.body:
Gambusia holbrooki will colonize any vegetated marginal wetland within its geographic range and is generally associated with various aquatic plants.  This species is least abundant over shallow bare bottoms and is more numerous where significant marginal vegetation exists (2372).  However, migrations across open periphyton mats etc., are common in ephemerally flooded salt marshes (2362) and freshwater glades (2371).  Larval and juvenile stages seek the shallowest water available (2365).

Substrate:  Found over muddy, sandy, or rocky bottom or shorelines, generally associated with aquatic vegetation (2372; 2365; 2362).

Physical/chemical:  The Eastern mosquitofish can tolerate an extreme range of physical parameters.  This species can survive in anaerobic waters by using aquatic surface respiration (2370).  Survival in fresh water to hypersaline conditions (0-80 ppt) has been documented (2363, pers. obs.).  Temperature range is from 5 to 37 C (702; 2379), however, the reproductive temperature range is from ca. 15.5 to 30 C (2365).

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body:
Reproductive Mode:  The Eastern mosquitofish is gonochoristic, polygamous, viviparous, and iteroparous; eggs are fertilized internally (2365).

Spawning Strategy:  Spawning occurs throughout its range with the length of reproductive activity varying with latitude and weather conditions (2365).  Multiple broods (from 2 to 8) are produced at intervals that average between 20.5 and 35 days during a breeding season.  Breeding occurs throughout the year in Florida with longer intervals between broods in the winter.  Activity peaks between March and October (2365).

Fecundity: Brood sizes are generally less than 50 but may reach 100 with published averages for the S. E. United States ranging from 11.3 to around 40 young.  Fecundity increases with increased size of the female (2365; 2373).

nodes.title: Length Range
nodes.body:
Egg:  Ripe ovarian eggs range in size from 1.6 to 2.1 mm with a yellow orange yolk, a thin vitelline membrane, and many small oil globules distributed near the entire surface (2365).  Gestation period averages 23.9 days (2365).

Juvenile:  Neonates are born at 6-8 mm as fully formed miniatures of the adult (Meffe pers. comm.)

Adult:  Size at maturity for males is ca. 15 to 28 mm (typically between 16 and 22 mm; Meffe pers. comm., 1992) with females maturing at 15 to 34.0 mm (typically 20-26 mm; 2365; Meffe pers. comm., 1992).  Age at maturity is temperature depended and ranges from 19 days to the second summer with males generally maturing first (2365; 2374).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: The Eastern mosquitofish is omnivorous but will selectively consume insect larvae when present.  Larval and juvenile stages prefer copepods while the adults facultatively consume plant material.  In the absence of abundant animal tissue, over 70% of food volume can be plant material (2366, 1982).

nodes.title: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
nodes.body: The Eastern mosquitofish is the most abundant and ubiquitous fish in fresh water in south Florida (2371).  It is also found in great numbers in brackish waters and has been collected in marginal wetlands of the Indian River Lagoon in salinities as high as 80 ppt (2363).  It is a Keystone species because of its reproductive potential and its ability to alter the habitats in which it occurs (2369).  The major factors controlling abundance and distribution are predation and the presence and density of vegetation.  This mosquitofish is an abundant food source for piscine and avian predators in numerous shallow habitats (2366; 2371) Gambusia holbrooki is a prime food source for larval and juvenile snook, Centropomus undecimalis in both freshwater and mangrove forest habitats (2366; 2378; 2364).

Life Mode:  This viviparous euryhaline schooling species typically feeds at or near the surface in shallow, still or slow moving waters generally associated with emergent vegetation or other structures (2365; 2363; 2371).  They may move offshore at night and may be found in water up to 3.6 m in depth.

sections.heading: Habitat Type
sections.content:
Gambusia holbrooki will colonize any vegetated marginal wetland within its geographic range and is generally associated with various aquatic plants.  This species is least abundant over shallow bare bottoms and is more numerous where significant marginal vegetation exists (2372).  However, migrations across open periphyton mats etc., are common in ephemerally flooded salt marshes (2362) and freshwater glades (2371).  Larval and juvenile stages seek the shallowest water available (2365).

Substrate:  Found over muddy, sandy, or rocky bottom or shorelines, generally associated with aquatic vegetation (2372; 2365; 2362).

Physical/chemical:  The Eastern mosquitofish can tolerate an extreme range of physical parameters.  This species can survive in anaerobic waters by using aquatic surface respiration (2370).  Survival in fresh water to hypersaline conditions (0-80 ppt) has been documented (2363, pers. obs.).  Temperature range is from 5 to 37 C (702; 2379), however, the reproductive temperature range is from ca. 15.5 to 30 C (2365).

sections.heading: REPRODUCTION
sections.content:
Reproductive Mode:  The Eastern mosquitofish is gonochoristic, polygamous, viviparous, and iteroparous; eggs are fertilized internally (2365).

Spawning Strategy:  Spawning occurs throughout its range with the length of reproductive activity varying with latitude and weather conditions (2365).  Multiple broods (from 2 to 8) are produced at intervals that average between 20.5 and 35 days during a breeding season.  Breeding occurs throughout the year in Florida with longer intervals between broods in the winter.  Activity peaks between March and October (2365).

Fecundity: Brood sizes are generally less than 50 but may reach 100 with published averages for the S. E. United States ranging from 11.3 to around 40 young.  Fecundity increases with increased size of the female (2365; 2373).

sections.heading: Length Range
sections.content:
Egg:  Ripe ovarian eggs range in size from 1.6 to 2.1 mm with a yellow orange yolk, a thin vitelline membrane, and many small oil globules distributed near the entire surface (2365).  Gestation period averages 23.9 days (2365).

Juvenile:  Neonates are born at 6-8 mm as fully formed miniatures of the adult (Meffe pers. comm.)

Adult:  Size at maturity for males is ca. 15 to 28 mm (typically between 16 and 22 mm; Meffe pers. comm., 1992) with females maturing at 15 to 34.0 mm (typically 20-26 mm; 2365; Meffe pers. comm., 1992).  Age at maturity is temperature depended and ranges from 19 days to the second summer with males generally maturing first (2365; 2374).

sections.heading: FOOD HABITS
sections.content: The Eastern mosquitofish is omnivorous but will selectively consume insect larvae when present.  Larval and juvenile stages prefer copepods while the adults facultatively consume plant material.  In the absence of abundant animal tissue, over 70% of food volume can be plant material (2366, 1982).

sections.heading: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
sections.content: The Eastern mosquitofish is the most abundant and ubiquitous fish in fresh water in south Florida (2371).  It is also found in great numbers in brackish waters and has been collected in marginal wetlands of the Indian River Lagoon in salinities as high as 80 ppt (2363).  It is a Keystone species because of its reproductive potential and its ability to alter the habitats in which it occurs (2369).  The major factors controlling abundance and distribution are predation and the presence and density of vegetation.  This mosquitofish is an abundant food source for piscine and avian predators in numerous shallow habitats (2366; 2371) Gambusia holbrooki is a prime food source for larval and juvenile snook, Centropomus undecimalis in both freshwater and mangrove forest habitats (2366; 2378; 2364).
